title: All scripture (2 Timothy 3:14–17)
hook: scripture is inspired and useful for teaching and correcting (CCC 105)

segments.voice: Yesterday, coals under the ash, and a gift fanned back into flame. Your line was fanned back into flame. Which gift did you use? Day five hundred ninety-six.

Hold your hand in front of your mouth and breathe out slowly. Warm, moving, there and then gone. Today's word is inspiration, the word the Church uses for what it teaches about the Bible. Behind it stands a single Greek word, near the end of the second letter to Timothy. Paul is reminding his young friend of the scriptures he has known since he was a child, and then he says what they are.
screen: `BREATHE ON YOUR HAND.` → `TODAY'S WORD: INSPIRATION.` → `ONE GREEK WORD IN SECOND TIMOTHY.`

segments.voice: From infancy, Paul says, you have known the holy scriptures. For Timothy, that meant the Jewish scriptures, what Christians call the Old Testament; the New was still being written. Then: "All scripture, inspired of God, is profitable to teach, to reprove, to correct, to instruct in justice, That the man of God may be perfect, furnished to every good work." Inspired of God is one Greek word: theopneustos. Theos, God. Pneō, to breathe. God-breathed. It may remind a reader of Genesis, where God breathes into the first man and he becomes a living soul. In that picture, the words on the page carry God's breath. Then four uses. To teach and to reprove are about what to believe. To correct and to instruct in justice are about how to live. Scripture, here, isn't a museum piece. It's a working tool, so the person of God is equipped for every good work. What do Catholics mean by inspiration? The Catechism says God is the author of Sacred Scripture. But the Second Vatican Council adds something important: the human writers were true authors too. God chose them and used them with their own powers and abilities, their language, their style, their era. So a reader can hear Paul's temper and Luke's careful research and the psalmist's grief, and the Church still calls the words God's. The Council says the books teach firmly, faithfully and without error the truth God wanted put into writing for the sake of our salvation. And it says Scripture must be read in the same Spirit in which it was written. For Catholics, that means reading it within the Church, together with Tradition. Breathed out once, the Church says, and breathed in every time it's read.
screen: `TIMOTHY'S SCRIPTURES.` · `THEOPNEUSTOS: GOD-BREATHED.` · `TEACH, REPROVE, CORRECT, INSTRUCT.` · `GOD AND HUMAN AUTHORS, BOTH TRUE.` · then, large: `ALL SCRIPTURE, INSPIRED OF GOD.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: read one verse slowly. Choose any verse you know, or use today's: all scripture, inspired of God. Settle, and breathe. Say it once, slowly, in your head. Then again, and notice which word stands out. Then a third time, and stay with that one word. Let it rise and fall with your breath, breathed in, breathed out. Don't analyze it. Just let it be read. If you pray, you can answer the word with a word of your own. If you don't, simply notice what one slow verse does to the next minute. The bell holds the time.
Inspiration. From the Greek theopneustos, God-breathed: Catholics believe Scripture has God as its author, written through true human authors. Today's word.
Your line: god-breathed. Today, read one verse three times, slowly, and carry the word that stood out. Day five hundred ninety-six.

screen: `DAY 596 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: I HAVE KEPT THE FAITH.`

howItsDone: Catholics hear Scripture at every Mass and many practice lectio divina, slow prayerful reading; the Church teaches that Scripture is inspired by God and is read within the living Tradition of the Church.

original.note: Greek: God-breathed, from theos (God) and pneō (to breathe), in 2 Timothy 3:16.

trapdoor: what you thought: inspiration means the writers felt inspired.
what it means: Scripture is God-breathed, with God as its author, written through true human authors.
what a scholar hears: theopneustos, God-breathed; Dei Verbum 11 on God and human authors; Timothy's scripture was the Jewish Bible.

sources.quoted: All scripture, inspired of God, is profitable to teach, to reprove, to correct, to instruct in justice, That the man of God may be perfect, furnished to every good work.

notes: theopneustos occurs only in 2 Timothy 3:16. Confirm.
Dei Verbum 11 ('true authors'; 'firmly, faithfully and without error ... for the sake of our salvation') and 12 (read in the same Spirit) paraphrased. Confirm.
Grouping the four uses as two about belief and two about life is an interpretive aid. Confirm acceptable.
